To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the correlation between central retinal thickness and BCVA is only found when the central foveal region is involved, and even in these cases, the correlation is only moderate.
central retinal thickness measured by HD-OCT is not strongly correlated with visual acuity, even in eyes with clinically important macular oedemas.
the correlations between central retinal thickness and visual acuity in diabetic macular oedemas were weak and only present when the macular oedematous area was larger than 500-μM diameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the correlation of retinal thickness measured using spectral domain high-definition OCT and visual acuity.
the correlation between retinal thickening and visual acuity.

the correlation between retinal thickness (measured using spectral-domain high definition optical coherence tomography) and best-correct visual acuity in patients with clinically significant macula oedema (a type of diabetic eye disease).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cirrus HD OCT central retinal thickness measurements are not a surrogate for best corrected visual acuity in patients with clinically significant macula edema.
the correlation between RT and visual acuity is weak in the majority of cases and that RT is not a good surrogate outcome for visual function.
there is a weak correlation between RT and VA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cirrus HD OCT is not a useful tool to monitor visual outcome in eyes with CSMD.
central retinal thickness (Cirrus OCT) and central point thickness (Stratus OCT) are not good surrogates of visual acuity in patients with clinically significant macula oedema.
the correlation between RT and VA is not strong enough to use the RT as a surrogate for visual outcome in clinical trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cirrus HD OCT is a useful tool for identifying retinal thickening and can be used to monitor treatment response in patients with clinically significant macula edema (CSME).
the Cirrus HD OCT is a very useful tool for the management of CSME.
RT measured by HD-OCT in CSME is only weakly associated with BCVA and, therefore, cannot be used as a reliable surrogate outcome measure in trials of treatments for this condition.
